channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
ttl3d turns RDF (Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, TriG, N-Quads) or a SPARQL CONSTRUCT
result into a single self-contained HTML page that shows the graph in 3D or 2D, with a legend,
label search and a detail card per node. The page inlines all of its JavaScript (a bundle of
three.js and force-graph, whose licenses ship in ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md), so it opens from
disk and works offline. A Python API shows the same page inline in Jupyter.
about.summary: Turn any Turtle / RDF graph into a self-contained, offline 2D/3D HTML viewer

script: python -c "from pathlib import Path; assert '<title>tiny</title>' in Path('page.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')"

name: ttl3d
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: 0.8.1

package:
  name: ttl3d
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/t/ttl3d/ttl3d-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: cc6e56178873e007115a78e2899a0ad5b4296a83c91e3426712732a3a7d7f279

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  python:
    entry_points:
      - ttl3d = ttl3d.cli:main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools >=68
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - rdflib >=7
    - networkx >=3
    - numpy
    - scipy

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - ttl3d
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    script:
      - ttl3d --version
      - python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('tiny.ttl').write_text('<http://example.org/a> <http://example.org/p> <http://example.org/b> .', encoding='utf-8')"
      - ttl3d tiny.ttl -o page.html
      - python -c "from pathlib import Path; assert '<title>tiny</title>' in Path('page.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')"

about:
  homepage: https://soheilabadifard.github.io/TTL_to_3D/
  repository: https://github.com/soheilabadifard/TTL_to_3D
  summary: Turn any Turtle / RDF graph into a self-contained, offline 2D/3D HTML viewer
  description: |
    ttl3d turns RDF (Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, TriG, N-Quads) or a SPARQL CONSTRUCT
    result into a single self-contained HTML page that shows the graph in 3D or 2D, with a legend,
    label search and a detail card per node. The page inlines all of its JavaScript (a bundle of
    three.js and force-graph, whose licenses ship in ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md), so it opens from
    disk and works offline. A Python API shows the same page inline in Jupyter.
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - soheilabadifard
